Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG: request for current subprocessors and supporting evidence

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking our call earlier. As part of Acme's procurement SIG intake, we need a consolidated list of Redwood's subprocessors and current evidence (SOC 2 scope, encryption attestations, support/tool vendors, telemetry processors). Can you share: 

- A single spreadsheet listing each subprocessor, purpose, data classification, country of processing, and contract status (POC + last attestation date).
- Copies of any vendor attestations or evidence (SOC 2 reports, DPAs, or equivalent).
- Any notes on telemetry vendors that receive aggregated production traces or metrics, and whether telemetry is PII-free.

We are aiming to complete review by 2027-04-15. If you can upload materials to our secure intake or share a Drive link, that works.

Appreciate it —Elaine
Elaine Morris
Senior Security Manager, Acme Corp
security@acmecorp.com

Subject: Re: SIG: request for current subprocessors and supporting evidence

Elaine —

Thanks for the clear list. I’m looping in Vanessa (Compliance lead) and Rishi (Security/infrastructure) to pull the canonical inventory and evidence package. We’ll aim to get a consolidated spreadsheet and initial evidence bundle to you by 2027-04-08.

Quick notes:
- We treat telemetry pipelines as non-PII by default; where we ingest customer-sent data that could be PII we have explicit flags and retention controls.
- Primary cloud providers: AWS (us-east-1/us-west-2), GCP for backups in eu-west-1, plus a telemetry pipe via LogStream (vendor).

Attach: placeholder for the inventory file (we will upload final).

Next steps for us: Vanessa, can you confirm which vendors need separate signed attestations and push the upload to the Drive link below? Rishi — please surface any recent SOC 2 or vendor-specific attestations you have.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber

Hi Jonas / Vanessa,

Attaching our signed SIG response and brief data handling summary. Key points:
- Purpose: aggregated telemetry ingestion for metrics and traces.
- Data types: application metrics, trace IDs, sampled spans. No customer PII is retained by default; payloads containing user IDs are hashed at ingestion per our contract.
- Region: US and EU processing available; EU processing on request.

Attachments: logstream-signed-sig-response.pdf (signed), logstream-data-handling.txt (summary).

If Acme needs a completed vendor questionnaire in their intake form, happy to coordinate directly.

Elaine — attaching the consolidated inventory and initial evidence package. See Drive link and attached spreadsheet. Summary below:

- redwood_subprocessors_master_v1.xlsx: contains columns [subprocessor, purpose, data_classification, region, contract_status, last_attestation]
- Evidence package: SOC 2 Type II summary (redacted PDF), DPAs (where applicable), LogStream signed sig response (attached by LogStream), and a telemetry controls checklist.

Open items for Acme to confirm:
1) Support tooling: we use Zendesk for ticketing and Intercom for in-app support sessions; for privacy-sensitive deployments Intercom is disabled and tickets are routed to Zendesk only.
2) Telemetry: LogStream receives aggregated traces; we also push anonymized metrics to a SaaS metrics vendor (Metricly) — note Metricly only receives aggregated counters and percentiles, not raw payloads.

Drive upload: https://drive.google.com/redwood/subprocessors/2027/q1 (link shared with acme security via restricted share)

Attachments included in upload: redwood_subprocessors_master_v1.xlsx, evidence-package-20270407.zip

Action items: Rishi, can you confirm the last SOC 2 snapshot date and whether Metricly has an addendum on data handling?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz

Vanessa / Elaine / team —

Confirmed: latest SOC 2 Type II coverage snapshot is 2027-02-28. I uploaded a redacted summary into the evidence-package-20270407.zip on the Drive link Vanessa provided.

Notes on two flagged vendors:
- Metricly (metrics vendor): no PII; we have an addendum that restricts data retention to 90 days and prevents raw payload export. I’ve attached the addendum stub in the evidence ZIP.
- Intercom (support): in standard deployments Intercom sees user identifiers for routing; for regulated customers we disable Intercom and route to Zendesk only. We have DPAs for both vendors.

Elaine — if you want a one-page attestation letter from our compliance team summarizing the telemetry and support handling differences for regulated vs standard deployments, I can generate that by 2027-04-10.

Best,
